{{Short description|53rd season of the National Hurling League}} {{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}} {{Infobox GAA League |league = 1983–84 National Hurling League |image = |dates = 2 October 1983 – 8 April 1984 |teams = |team1 = Limerick |captain1 = |manager1 = |titles = 8th |team2 = |captain2 = |manager2 = |two = Tipperary |three = Roscommon |four = Longford |previous = [[1982–83 National Hurling League|1982–83]] |next = [[1984–85 National Hurling League|1984–85]] }} The '''1983–84 National Hurling League''' was the 53rd season of the [[National Hurling League]]. ==Division 1== {{Infobox football league season |competition=[[National Hurling League|National Hurling League Division 1]] |season=1983-84 |winners=[[Limerick GAA|Limerick]]

[[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] |continentalcup1= |continentalcup1 qualifiers= |continentalcup2= |continentalcup2 qualifiers= |league topscorer=[[File: Colours of Kilkenny.svg|border|20px]] [[Billy Fitzpatrick]] |best goalkeeper= |biggest home win= |biggest away win= |highest scoring= |matches= 36 |total goals= |longest wins= |longest unbeaten= |longest winless= |longest losses= |highest attendance= |lowest attendance= |attendance= |average attendance= |prevseason=[[1982–83 National Hurling League|1982–83]] |nextseason=[[1984–85 National Hurling League|1984–85]] |updated=6 March 2017 }} [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] came into the season as defending champions of the [[1982-83 National Hurling League|1982-83 season]]. On 8 April 1984, [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] won the title after a 3-16 to 1-9 win over [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] in the final.
